name: Digital SAT
description: College Board Digital SAT exam testing Reading & Writing and Math.

difficulty_scale.label: Easy
difficulty_scale.definition: Direct, single-step questions testing fundamental rules or clear facts. Solvable in under 30 seconds by a student who knows the underlying rule.

difficulty_scale.label: Medium
difficulty_scale.definition: Multi-step questions requiring analytical interpretation, simple translation, or combining 2-3 rules. Solvable in about 60-75 seconds with no unusual insight required.

difficulty_scale.label: Hard
difficulty_scale.definition: Calibrated to the hardest ~10% of REAL Digital SAT questions (Math: the last 1-2 questions of a module) — NOT competition math or graduate-level content. A Hard question requires the student to synthesize 2-3 skills from the SAME curriculum used for Easy/Medium (Algebra I/II, Geometry, basic trig, stats — no calculus, no obscure theorems), spot a non-obvious first step, translate an unusually wordy or abstractly-framed scenario, or eliminate deliberately close/high-nuance distractors. It must remain solvable by a well-prepared high schooler in roughly 90-120 seconds by hand or with a basic calculator, using clean-ish numbers (no need for a page of algebra or ugly fractions/decimals). Difficulty must come from the REASONING/INSIGHT required, not from added computational grind, unfamiliar vocabulary/notation, extra variables for their own sake, or content outside the standard SAT Math curriculum.

style_rules: Do not duplicate real official College Board questions or passages.
For Reading & Writing: Passages should be dense, academic, and between 50-150 words.
For Math: Stimulus can be word problems, linear/nonlinear system parameters, geometric descriptions, or function formulas.
Distractors must be highly plausible, capturing typical errors (e.g., sign errors, misinterpreting variables, using opposite transitions, or choosing partially correct answers).

checks.description: Is the marked correct answer mathematically or textually verified as 100% accurate?
Are distractors realistic, non-obvious, and derived from common student mistakes? Is there absolutely NO secondary defensible correct answer?
Is the text grammatical, free of typos, and completely unambiguous?
Does the complexity match the requested easy/medium/hard definition?
Does the question test the selected domain and skill specifically?
Does the question stand alone without copying existing bank items or copyrighted sources?
Is the question free of cultural, regional, socio-economic biases, and sensitive topics?
